A_axis: early-season flower redness
candidate_measure: CH fruits per plant per day; seeds per CH fruit
status_or_result: verified_two_component_interaction_terms
reason: A_z:D_z is explicitly fit on two reproductive components. D role is supported by linked same-species evidence that floral condensed tannins are associated with lower nectar robbing/thieving/florivory. Trait effects remain observational and both interaction CIs overlap zero.

A_axis: floral traits associated with distyly/pollination
candidate_measure: visitor outcomes
status_or_result: no_AxD_term_verified
reason: Models include separate trait main effects and trait-by-site/morph terms rather than an attraction-by-defence interaction. Joint measurement alone is insufficient.

A_axis: total floral scent
candidate_measure: eaten flowers per total flowers
status_or_result: no_D_axis
reason: Strong quantitative A-to-antagonism effect exists, but no distinct D trait is available in the linked panel.

A_axis: floral attraction/resin context
candidate_measure: candidate reproductive/visitor outcomes
status_or_result: not_identifiable
reason: Historical audit found no defensible collection identifiers linking bee-response data to the floral trait matrix. No guessed linkage is allowed.

A_axis: petal colour polymorphism
candidate_measure: trait/defence responses
status_or_result: no_direct_AxD_fitness_term_verified
reason: The paper links pollinator-associated floral colour with defence architecture but does not identify the direct A x D reproductive interaction or shared allocation cost needed for Tier 1 or kappa.

A_axis: UV floral pattern
candidate_measure: caterpillar feeding
status_or_result: no_distinct_A_and_D_axes
reason: Signal and defence roles are carried by the same pigment chemistry, not two declared focal axes. Dual-function single-trait evidence cannot instantiate an A x D interaction.

A_axis: benzylacetone floral scent production
candidate_measure: Manduca oviposition; pollinator-mediated seed production
status_or_result: fully_crossed_2x2_but_no_reported_factorial_interaction_term
reason: RNAi independently silences scent (CHAL) and nectar production (SWEET9), including the double-silenced cross, but the second axis is a pollinator reward rather than an independently justified flower-specific defence/access trait. The paper compares four lines with Friedman/pairwise tests rather than an uncertainty-bearing scent x nectar interaction. Public supplement audit run 31457174360/artifact 9088554499 recovered only three TIFF figure supplements and no raw Figure-2 outcome table. Reclassifying no-nectar as D solely because it reduces oviposition would violate the orientation gate.

A_axis: banner petal width and length plus reproductive display traits
candidate_measure: relative reproductive fitness under crossed herbivory and pollination
status_or_result: verified floral_trait_x_HCN terms and floral_trait_x_HCN_x_herbivory interactions
reason: This is a genuine near-direct interaction design: e.g. banner width x HCN x herbivory P=0.014 and banner length x HCN x herbivory P=0.046. However HCN is a Mendelian whole-plant antiherbivore defence rather than a separately demonstrated flower-specific D axis under the active protocol. Treating it as strict floral D would silently relax the organ gate.

A_axis: plant size; flower number; frost tolerance; inflorescence density
D_axis: five defence-related metabolites from leaf metabolomics
candidate_measure: total seed output
status_or_result: trait_x_pollination_and_trait_x_herbivory_context_terms_but_no_A_trait_x_D_trait_term
reason: The full model estimates how pollination and herbivory alter selection on each of nine attraction/defence traits. Defence metabolites came from leaf sampling and only 27 genotypes had metabolomic data. No attraction-trait x defence-trait interaction is specified; ecological-agent interactions are not equivalent to A x D.

A_axis: plant/inflorescence size; petal width; nectar reward traits
candidate_measure: pollinia insertion/removal; fruit production
status_or_result: original_selection_models_main_effects_only_and_no_AxD_term
reason: This source passes the organ and individual-linkage gates unusually well because floral latex is measured separately from leaf latex on the same plants as floral attraction traits. However the published phenotypic-selection model contains the ten standardized trait main effects only. The authors state that they lacked statistical power to detect non-linear selection and excluded those analyses. Adding petal-width x floral-latex or another correlational-selection term now would therefore be an unplanned post-hoc model rather than recovery of a source-identified A x D effect. No florivory was observed, so the ecological driver of positive selection on floral latex also remains unresolved.

A_axis: corolla size; phenylacetaldehyde and other floral signals
candidate_measure: visitation; oviposition; fruit-set selection
status_or_result: correlational_selection_among_A_traits_and_nonadditive_mutualist_antagonist_selection_but_no_AxD_axis
reason: The study is highly informative for attraction tracking: corolla size and phenylacetaldehyde attract both pollinators and Pieris oviposition, and combined insects generate nonadditive selection. But there is no separately measured/manipulated defence trait D; an antagonist treatment is not a D phenotype.

A_axis: petal size; floral display; pollinator-use traits
D_axis: high versus low myrosinase artificial-selection lines with documented flea-beetle resistance
candidate_measure: pollinator visitation; flowers visited; time per flower
status_or_result: resistance_x_damage_changes_floral_traits_and_pollinator_use_but_no_flower_A_trait_x_D_trait_term_verified
reason: Artificial selection produced high- and low-myrosinase lines with corresponding flea-beetle resistance, and high resistance plus herbivore damage altered floral traits and pollinator foraging. This is strong ecological-cost evidence linking defence architecture to pollination, but the resistance treatment is a whole-plant selection regime rather than an independently established flower-specific D phenotype, and the accessible source does not identify an attraction-trait x defence-trait fitness interaction.

A_axis: inflorescence colour and pollination syndrome morphology
D_axis: floral cyanide plus physical foliage/spine protection
candidate_measure: comparative trait covariation across bird- and insect-pollinated species
status_or_result: comparative_A_D_covariation_without_within_system_AxD_outcome
reason: Across 51 Hakea species, bird/insect pollination covaries with floral colour and physical/chemical defence architecture, including floral cyanide. This is a valuable macroevolutionary A-D covariance pattern but does not estimate an A x D interaction on pollination, antagonism or reproduction within linked biological units.

A_axis: pollinator-attractive components of the floral volatile bouquet
D_axis: distinct defensive floral-scent compounds reducing generalist florivory
candidate_measure: florivore damage across transgenic scent-silencing lines
status_or_result: different_bouquet_components_partition_attractive_and_defensive_functions_but_no_AxD_interaction_term
reason: Five transgenic Petunia lines silencing particular floral volatile components show that some bouquet compounds contribute to host location whereas others reduce florivore damage. The system demonstrates component-level division of labour inside one floral blend, but it does not estimate the interaction between a declared attraction axis and a distinct defence axis on a common outcome.

A_axis: floral attractive/reward traits: corolla length; pollen; nectar; volatile classes
candidate_measure: Pearson correlations between defensive and attractive/reward traits as an explicit allocation-tradeoff test
status_or_result: No correlations between leaf or floral cucurbitacins and any floral attractive/reward trait; |r|<0.25 and P>0.05 for all
reason: The authors explicitly test an allocation-tradeoff prediction, but trait covariance is not a measurement of construction/allocation cost. A null covariance cannot be interpreted as kappa=0.

A_axis: floral_scent_volatiles
candidate_measure: phenotypic integration/correlation across compound groups
status_or_result: Between-group integration was low; authors conclude no evidence that integration between attractive and defensive compound groups strongly constrains diversification
reason: The study tests evolutionary integration rather than resource expenditure. The D axes are foliar rather than flower-specific, and low integration means evolutionary independence, not absence of a direct joint construction cost.

A_axis: petal_colour_polymorphism
candidate_measure: association of colour morph and constitutive/induced secondary chemistry; possible pleiotropy or tight linkage discussed
status_or_result: Petal colour morph is associated with aspects of inducibility/secondary chemistry architecture, but no direct resource or construction-cost variable and no A x D allocation term is measured
reason: Genetic linkage or pleiotropy can generate trait covariance without an energetic allocation cost. This study therefore cannot identify kappa.

A_axis: petal size; floral display; pollinator reward/use proxies
D_axis: artificially selected high versus low myrosinase herbivore resistance
candidate_measure: ecological cost of resistance expressed through altered floral traits and pollinator foraging
status_or_result: High-resistance plants developed smaller petals later in life; floral display also depended on resistance x damage; pollinators spent more time per flower on low-resistance plants while total pollinator attraction did not differ
reason: The paper deliberately studies an ecological cost of resistance in the currency of pollination. That maps to defence effects on mutualist use / floral phenotype, not to a measured resource term depending jointly on an attraction trait and flower-specific D. Labeling every 'cost of resistance' as kappa would confound iota-like ecological interference with direct allocation/construction cost.

A_axis: floral fragrance and pollinator-attractive floral phenotype
candidate_measure: experimental evolution under bee versus hand pollination crossed with herbivory; reduced evolution of attractive floral signals under herbivory interpreted as likely physiological trade-off/resource reallocation
status_or_result: Herbivory compromised evolution of attractive flowers and altered defence traits, but the physiological link between defence compounds, floral signals and rewards was explicitly left for further investigation
reason: The design manipulates selection agents, not a fixed A+D resource budget. Resource reallocation is a plausible explanation among physiological mechanisms, not a directly measured joint construction cost.

A_axis: floral VOCs and morphology affecting pollinator attraction
candidate_measure: herbivory changes floral signals and pollinator/parasitoid attraction; resource allocation or physiological cross-talk discussed as possible mechanisms
status_or_result: Herbivory alters floral phenotype and insect attraction, but the source does not directly measure the resource/energetic price of jointly producing attraction and flower-specific defence
reason: An induced decline in floral signalling can arise through allocation, hormonal cross-talk, damage, phenology or adaptive plasticity. Without direct resource accounting it cannot identify kappa.

A_axis: reproductive output and correlated floral traits
D_axis: foliar glucosinolate content selected high versus low
candidate_measure: fitness/correlated responses used to test costs of defence
status_or_result: A marginal cost of foliar defence can be tested through divergent glucosinolate selection, but no distinct floral A axis is jointly budgeted with a flower-specific D axis
reason: A demonstrated D cost is not the A+D interaction cost. The defence is also foliar rather than flower-specific under the active protocol.

A_axis: nectar sugar/reward and pollinator visitation
candidate_measure: dose-dependent ecological costs of nectar alkaloids; allocation/transport costs discussed as possible explanations for low nectar concentrations
status_or_result: Low nectar-alkaloid concentrations can have little ecological pollinator cost, while the paper discusses rather than measures allocation costs to nectar secondary metabolites
reason: The study identifies a flower-specific D axis and ecological effects, but it does not measure plant expenditure on D or an additional cost of producing D together with a separate attraction trait.

A_axis: nectar sugar reward concentration
D_axis: defensive plant phenolics added to nectar
candidate_measure: bee feeding assays suggest phenolic-rich nectar could maintain attraction at lower sugar reward and therefore reduce plant expenditure
status_or_result: Phenolics interact nonlinearly with sugar and authors propose a lower-cost pollinator reward strategy, but actual plant resource expenditure is not measured
reason: This is a functional-substitution/energy-saving hypothesis derived from pollinator behaviour. It does not directly quantify plant savings, and A and D are not independently manipulated as production investments in a plant.

A_axis: floral resin reward amount/display to resin-collecting pollinators
D_axis: ancestral defensive function of resin/exaptation context
candidate_measure: direct experimental test of resin reward production cost through reduced seed production when pollinators cannot harvest resin
status_or_result: Resin reward production imposes a measurable reproductive cost, but reward and defence are functions of the same material rather than two distinct A and D investments
reason: This is strong direct evidence that an attractive/reward trait can be costly and an important evolutionary exaptation case. It identifies an A marginal cost, not curvature from simultaneous investment in distinct A and D axes.

A_axis: pollen/pollen-presenter structures with reproductive function
candidate_measure: fine-scale allocation of defensive chemistry among high-value floral tissues
status_or_result: Very high cyanogenic-glycoside concentrations are localized to pollen/anthers and pollen-presenter tissues, demonstrating targeted flower-specific defence allocation but not its energetic cost or covariance with an attraction investment
reason: Optimal placement of D within flowers is not joint A+D resource accounting. No distinct attraction trait or construction-cost interaction is measured.

A_axis: floral advertisement chemistry exists in the system but is not jointly costed in this experiment
D_axis: flower-specific jasmonate-regulated TPI bergamotene and defensin defences
candidate_measure: molecular dissection of flower-specific defence regulation and tissue allocation
status_or_result: A flower-specific JA sector controls multiple constitutive floral defences, establishing that D can be regulated independently at the organ level; no A+D energy/resource interaction is measured
reason: Mechanistic regulation of flower defence answers where/how D is produced, not what additional resource cost arises from simultaneously producing attraction and D.

A_axis: male flower production; pollen; nectar; floral VOC pollinator cues
D_axis: defence is induced by simulated foliar damage rather than a measured flower-specific D phenotype
candidate_measure: mechanical damage reduces reproductive/floral investment and is interpreted through possible resource reallocation to defence
status_or_result: Early-season damage changes flower production and pollinator-relevant floral traits, but resource reallocation toward defence is a mechanistic hypothesis and no flower-specific D expenditure is directly measured
reason: Agent-induced reduction in A or reproduction is not an A+D joint construction-cost measurement. This source maps to the already adjudicated induced-reallocation class.
